## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The deleted defaults file must be restored or its loader updated before merge because calling the existing loader now raises `FileNotFoundError`. Tests were assessed by reading them; no tests were run.

## Changes
The pull request adds millisecond timeout parsing, port validation, JSON configuration loading, host normalization, and tests. It also deletes the bundled defaults file and adds reviewer documentation and a review fixture.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Restore the bundled defaults or update its loader — Calling `load_defaults()` now raises `FileNotFoundError` because this deletion leaves `app/startup.py:6` reading a nonexistent `defaults.json`. — Users of the existing defaults loader lose access to the default timeout and receive an exception instead.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — Accept port 65535 — For `is_valid_port(65535)`, the function returns `False` even though its documented range includes 65535; the upper comparison excludes that endpoint. — Users configuring TCP port 65535 receive an incorrect validation failure.

- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — Make configuration loading failures identifiable — For a malformed JSON configuration file, `except Exception` discards the decoding error and returns `{}` without logging or signaling failure. The docstring does not explain this fallback. — Callers cannot distinguish a broken configuration from a successfully loaded empty configuration, preventing actionable diagnosis.

- app/parse.py:40 — tests — Cover trailing-dot host normalization — For `normalize_host("Example.COM.")`, no test exercises the trailing-dot removal branch; the sole normalization test uses `"Example.COM"`. — A regression that preserves trailing dots would pass the existing tests and leave fully qualified hosts inconsistently normalized.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — Align the documented empty-host result — For `normalize_host("")`, the docstring promises “returns None when h is empty,” but the empty-input branch executes `return ""`. — Callers following the documented `None` sentinel will handle empty host values incorrectly.
